scope_change_request.approval_note: approval_state is the SINGLE authoritative state. The procedure edits exactly these four fields; the binding gate consults only approval_state, approved_by, approved_at and approved_scope (which must equal expected_approved_scope). There is no second status field, so following the procedure cannot be rejected by a state the procedure never sets.
scope_change_request.approver_role: operator (scope approval) + a reviewer other than the author (code/assertion/receipt review)
scope_change_request.binding_rule: this request is part of the payload identity B. Approving it means editing approval_state/approved_scope/approved_by/approved_at in this payload, which PRODUCES A NEW B. A market run must use the protocol fingerprint of the B that carries the APPROVED state; any later payload edit produces a new B and invalidates the approval, requiring a fresh approval before the run.

ledger.evaluation_attempt_roots: the runner creates cell_attempts/<uuid>/ per ATTEMPT; the attempt history of one evaluation is the set of attempt roots whose recorded identity hashes to that evaluation's cache key.
ledger.evaluation_vs_attempt: the cache key identifies the EVALUATION (one planned cell). The worker's cell_execution/<uuid>/ directories under the runner's attempt directory are the ATTEMPTS of that evaluation. One row is written per evaluation (cell_ledger/<key>.json) with the attempt count and the attempt outcomes, so a retried or resumed evaluation stays ONE evaluation and is never counted twice.
ledger.fresh_cache_failure: the row records the execution path (fresh or cache_hit) and the artifact status; a cache hit has no attempt root of its own and is classified from the attempt history already on disk.
ledger.interrupted_requires_stopped_process: INTERRUPTED requires the worker process to be gone; a missing result.json while the worker is alive is RUNNING, not INTERRUPTED
ledger.latest_attempt_ordering: by the producer's real start time (started_at_epoch, falling back to the ISO started_at); never by directory name. The worker and the runner both write started_at_epoch.
ledger.ledger_failure_not_silent: a ledger write failure is appended to cell_ledger/_ledger_errors.jsonl (durable, append-only) and logged loudly; it is never only printed.
ledger.ledger_merge: one row per evaluation, MERGED across its attempts: the row keeps the attempt history and updates the counts and the outcome, so a retried or resumed evaluation stays one evaluation.
ledger.no_reconciler_function: there is no separate reconciler function in the codebase: the reconciliation is the runner-layer cell_failures record plus the absence of a completion receipt (exact_coverage.json / parallel_canonical_summary.json), and the coverage verification fails closed when a fold is not SELECTed.
ledger.reconciler_note: there is no separate reconciler function in the codebase: the reconciliation is the runner-layer cell_failures record plus the absence of a completion receipt (exact_coverage.json / parallel_canonical_summary.json), and the coverage verification fails closed when a fold is not SELECTed.
ledger.reconciliation_rule: the two layers are linked by the cache key: the runner's attempt directory holds the worker's cell_execution/<uuid>/ directory. The worker writes started.json BEFORE execution and result.json AFTER it -- and it writes the result even when the cell failed, so the result carries the artifact and its status. Therefore: an attempt is COMPLETED when result.json exists and its artifact status is COMPLETED; FAILED when result.json exists and the artifact is not completed; and INTERRUPTED only when result.json is MISSING AND the worker process is GONE. While the worker process is still alive the attempt is RUNNING, not INTERRUPTED. The runner layer records the attempt start in cell_attempts/<key>/execution_started.json and the failure in cell_failures/<key>__<uuid>.json; the start record alone proves only that the attempt STARTED and is NOT sufficient to classify it.
ledger.verified_by: src/trading_agent/backtest/attempt_ledger.py implements the classification; the runner writes one evaluation-level row per cell.
